elements: central point P0 rendered as a small dark sphere with label 'P₀' beside it
vertical spindle (thin line/cylinder) passing through P0, oriented along the curl direction, with an arrowhead at the top
text label 'Curl F(P₀)' next to the arrowhead of the spindle
curved rotation arrow (open arc ~270° with arrowhead) encircling the upper portion of the spindle indicating counter-clockwise spin when viewed from above
four salmon-colored rectangular paddle blades radiating outward from P0 at 90-degree intervals around the spindle axis, each standing perpendicular to the spindle
set of 4–5 concentric partial arcs (broken strokes, ~200–260° each with gaps) in light blue lying in the plane perpendicular to the spindle through P0, indicating circular fluid flow
small gap between adjacent arcs to give a hand-drawn, non-closed appearance

interactions.teaches: Rotating the viewpoint confirms that the spindle, the curl arrow, and the rotation axis are all the same line — the curl vector IS the axle of maximum rotation

Moving P0 through the field re-evaluates Curl F at the new location: the spindle (which is the curl direction) reorients and rescales, showing that the axis of fastest paddle-wheel rotation changes from point to point and always equals the curl direction

interactions.label: Field scale k
interactions.teaches: Scaling the entire vector field scales the curl magnitude uniformly — the paddle wheel spins faster or slower but its axis direction stays the same, reinforcing that curl direction and magnitude are independent properties

demo_steps.title: Curl points up at P₀
demo_steps.narration: At the origin, Curl F(P₀) = (0, 2, 0) points straight up. The spindle, the curl arrow, and the rotation axis are all the same vertical line — the paddle wheel spins fastest with its axle aligned this way.

demo_steps.title: Scale the field
demo_steps.narration: Increase k to 2.5. The curl magnitude grows, the arrow lengthens, and the wheel spins faster — but the axis direction is unchanged. Curl direction and magnitude are separate properties.

demo_steps.title: Drag P₀ off-axis
demo_steps.narration: Drag P₀ to a position where y ≠ 0. The curl gains a z-component, so the spindle tilts away from vertical. The paddle wheel's axis of maximum rotation always follows the curl vector.

plan.geometry_notes: Vector field: F(x,y,z) = k·(z, x·y, −x) where k is the field-strength slider. Curl F = k·(0, 2, y). At default P₀=(0,0,0): Curl F = (0, 2k, 0), pointing straight up (+Y). Spindle: thin cylinder radius 0.03, length proportional to |Curl F| (display length = |Curl F| * 0.8, clamped to max 3.0), with cone arrowhead at top. Label 'Curl F(P₀)' offset to the right of the arrowhead. Rotation arrow: torus arc ~270° radius 0.35 at 80% of spindle height, with small cone arrowhead. Four blades: rectangles 1.0 unit long (radial) × 0.6 unit wide, inner edge at 0.15 from P₀, arranged at 0°/90°/180°/270° around the spindle axis, fill salmon #FA8072 with dark outline #333. Flow arcs: 5 partial arcs at radii 0.8, 1.2, 1.6, 2.0, 2.4 in the plane perpendicular to the curl at P₀. Each arc spans a random 200–260° with a gap, drawn as individual arc segments (not full circles). Color light blue #87CEEB, line width 1.5. P₀ sphere radius 0.06, color #222. World extent roughly ±3 in X and Z, ±3 in Y. Ground reference: none (floating in space).
plan.notes: Parent all paddle-wheel components (blades, spindle, rotation arrow, flow arcs) under a THREE.Group at P₀. On drag, recompute curl at new P₀, then set the group's quaternion so the spindle axis aligns with normalize(curl). The blades rotate about the local spindle axis each frame at angular speed proportional to |curl|. Flow arcs are rebuilt as partial THREE.EllipseCurve segments (not full circles) with gaps; orient the arc plane perpendicular to the curl direction using a lookAt or quaternion. Use LineDashedMaterial is NOT needed since arcs are already partial geometry — just use solid LineBasicMaterial on the partial arcs. The arrowhead on the spindle is the ONLY representation of the curl vector (no separate arrow).

authoredPrompt: This figure shows a physical analogy for the curl of a vector field at a point. At the center is a labeled point P0, around which concentric dashed blue arcs indicate a circular fluid flow pattern. Four paddle-like rectangular surfaces (salmon-colored) radiate outward from P0 like propeller blades. A vertical spindle passes through P0, and the vector Curl F(P0) labels an upward arrow along the spindle, with a curved arrow showing the direction of rotation. The figure provides the physical interpretation that a small paddle wheel immersed in the fluid at P0 rotates most rapidly when its spindle is aligned with curl F(P0), establishing the connection between the curl vector and the direction of maximum circulation density.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag point P₀ to a new location and display the updated Curl F(P₀) vector, showing how curl magnitude and direction vary across the field
- Slider for rotation rate: animate the paddle-wheel spinning and show how the curl vector magnitude corresponds to the angular speed of rotation
- Drag to rotate the 3D viewpoint to see the curl vector axis and paddle blades from any direction
authoredContext: We call curl F(P0) n the circulation density of F at P0 in the direction of n. This quantity has its maximum value when n is in the same direction as curl F(P0); this tells us that at each point in a steady-state fluid flow the maximum circulation density occurs in the direction of the curl. Physically, this means that if a small paddle wheel is immersed in the fluid so that the pivot point is at P0, then the paddles will turn most rapidly when the spindle is aligned with curl F(P0) (Figure 15.8.6). If curl F = 0 at each point of a region, then F is said to be irrotational in that region, since no circulation occurs about any point of the region
sourceQmd: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 15.8.6

interactions.label: Rotation rate omega
interactions.teaches: The paddle wheel spins at angular speed omega; matching omega to |Curl F(P0)| (the component of curl along the spindle) shows that the curl magnitude IS the circulation density / angular speed of the wheel when its axle is aligned with the curl
Rotating the viewpoint lets the learner see the spindle, the four blades edge-on and face-on, and confirm that the rotation arrow and the curl vector share the same axis

demo_steps.title: Aligned at P0
demo_steps.narration: At the default point the curl points straight up the spindle and the wheel spins fastest; the dashed arcs show the circular flow that drives it.

demo_steps.title: Tilt the curl
demo_steps.narration: Drag P0 sideways (e.g. +x, +y). The Curl F arrow tilts away from vertical and changes length, so a vertical spindle no longer captures the full circulation.

demo_steps.title: Match omega to |curl|
demo_steps.narration: Slide omega up or down and watch the wheel speed change; the readout confirms omega equals |Curl F(P0)| when the axle is aligned with the curl.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: paddle wheel assembly centered at P0. Use the sample field F(x,y,z) = (-y*(1+0.5*z), x*(1+0.5*z), 0.5*x*y), whose curl is Curl F = (0.5*x, -0.5*y, 2+z). Default P0 = (0,0,0) gives Curl F = (0,0,2) (vertical, length 2 world units) exactly matching the figure. Four blades at azimuths 0/90/180/270 deg about the vertical (curl) axis; each blade a vertical rectangle ~1.1 units radial (X-Z plane of the blade) by ~0.7 units tall, inner edge ~0.15 from P0, fill salmon #f3c0a8 with black #111 outline. Spindle: thin black cylinder/line from P0 up ~2.3 units with a cone arrowhead; curved rotation arrow as a ~270-deg arc of radius ~0.35 near the top with an arrowhead. Concentric dashed flow arcs in the horizontal plane through P0 at radii 0.7, 1.1, 1.5, 1.9, 2.3, light blue #7fc3e0, drawn as circles (become ellipses in view). When P0 is dragged, translate the whole assembly (blades+arcs+spindle) to P0 and recompute the curl arrow direction = normalize(Curl F(P0)) and length = |Curl F(P0)| (clamp display length to ~2.5). Readout shows |Curl F(P0)| = sqrt((0.5x)^2+(0.5y)^2+(2+z)^2). Colors: salmon blades #f3c0a8, blue arcs #7fc3e0, black spindle/arrow/labels #111111.
interactionPlan.notes: Parent the blades, dashed arcs, spindle and rotation arrow under a single THREE.Group anchored at P0 so the drag interaction translates the entire wheel rigidly; only the curl arrow's orientation/length and the readout are recomputed on drag. Animate blade rotation about the current spindle (curl) axis at omega rad/s each frame. Render flow arcs with LineDashedMaterial and call computeLineDistances(); rebuild them in the horizontal plane of P0. Keep the curl arrow as a separate object (cylinder + cone) so its direction can be set independently of the wheel group's spin. Use a perspective camera with moderate elevation so the horizontal arcs read as ellipses like the source.
